blocks: The owner's manual lists exactly one modular jack: '8P8C Modular Jack (Also called RJ-45 Jack) for connecting Remote Control Model NTX-RC'. The words Modbus, RS-485 and RS-232 do not appear in the manual. The NTX-RC is a bundled LCD remote on a proprietary link with no published protocol.
sharedMapEvidence: One vendor manual (11002-NTX-1000-1500-2000-3000-3000S-12-24) covers NTX-1000 through NTX-3000S in both 12 V and 24 V, and describes a single NTX-RC jack for all of them. A companion manual covers NTX-400/600. Grouping is by shared absence of a bus, not by a shared map.
gotchas: The retailer claim 'included wired remote' is accurate — §4.14: 'Remote Control Model NTX-RC has been provided with the unit.' That makes NTX look more connected than it is. It is a panel, not a port.

Interlock worth knowing if anyone ever automates around one: §4.14 warns that when NTX-RC is used, the inverter's own ON/OFF switch must be left OFF, otherwise switching off at the remote does not switch off the inverter.
Plain inverter, DeviceKind inverter. Monitor it the same way as any passive AC source: a PZEM or a Shelly downstream.
